function: Excluded, system: federated edge learning with over-the-air aggregation (area 7 by function) on a link where the server and the devices have a single antenna, no RIS (p. 3).
notes: Reason system (check 6). no_learning does not apply because the work is federated learning with over-the-air computation (AirComp), where the learned element is the model trained across the devices (p. 1, abstract: "the over-the-air computation (AirComp) technique is employed for a communication-efficient model aggregation"). The physical-layer part is the AirComp power control and denoising factor (P3, closed form, p. 8), so the function is area 7; above_phy does not apply because the optimized variables include the AirComp transmit power and denoising factor (physical layer) jointly with sensing and computing variables. The link has a single antenna and no RIS: p. 3: "both the edge server and the devices are equipped with a single antenna for signal transmission"; channel is block fading, p. 4. No RIS or multi-antenna array appears anywhere in the paper. The proposed method is classical optimization (block coordinate update plus Lyapunov, Algorithm 1, p. 9; complexity O(l_max (N^3.5 + N log N)) with l_max the iteration limit, p. 9); the neural network is trained on MNIST, FMNIST and a pedestrian-bicyclist dataset (p. 9). Alternative code for the reviewer: if the problem of the paper is judged to be the sensing-computation-communication resource allocation rather than the over-the-air aggregation itself, the code would be function; the decision stays exclude either way. Quantitative results exist (Figs. 2-7, pp. 9-11), so results is not the reason.
